::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 12th [1867]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Charlotte Mitchell
:::

My dear [Edith](people/person_749.qmd),
You will think there is no end to me but I saw [Mr Moore](people/person_1046.qmd) yesterday and he says that his magic lantern came from Carpenter & Newman 24 Regent Street, and that they are much better than Negretti having devoted their minds to magic lanterns His lamp is an Argand These were all your questions I could recollect, but if you have any more, he will gladly and <u>clearheadedly</u> answer them. [Mamma](people/person_1606.qmd) has just seen the new nursery maid trotting after the donkey carriage and ‘Mithter Dandatti’ and the three children & thought she looked very nice.[^1] On Saturday week [Miss Mackenzie](people/person_930.qmd) will betake herself to the Kings Head at Hursley. The American lady who wrote the Scilly isles wants to do a series of English cathedrals - it is like the Scotch lady flying at Archbishops.

Poor dear Field House we took leave of it and its roses and cows last night, and felt as if a very sunny page in our life was turned down[^2]

yours affectionately
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: This suggests that Edith Jacob had recommended a nursery maid to JBY’s family, and CMY is giving news of her progress.
[^3]: The farmhouse at Hursley which [Dr. George Moberly](people/person_1015.qmd) had rented from Sir William Heathcote, which his family were now leaving for ever.
